text:
Jack McBain is a third-line centre who hits everything, 84 times in 21 games. With Utah's top six thinned by injuries, his quieter offensive game has started to show up: a goal and two assists in Las Vegas, and another goal against San Jose on Saturday.

The chances have been there all season. He has 3 goals on 4.3 expected, and over his last ten games his shots have been dangerous enough to rank among the better depth forwards in the league by our numbers. Utah takes 58% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, a little better than without him, which is a change from last season, when Evolving-Hockey had him in the bottom 10% of forwards defensively.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds the shape of his game: he rarely carries the puck in (19% of entries), leaning on dump-ins and the forecheck, but he exits his own zone cleanly 71% of the time and gets shots off passes across the slot. Our talent range has him around 13 goals. On a team looking for depth scoring, that's worth watching.
